extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and institutional legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for designing and operating Title IX grievance procedures, including evidentiary limits (rape-shield), notice of allegations, permissible dismissals, procedural flexibility, training, and recordkeeping requirements for educational recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(b)(7)(iii) — Prohibition on evidence of complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must prohibit questioning about or consideration of a complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct throughout Title IX grievance procedures, subject only to narrowly drawn exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition aligns with rape-shield protections and is not governed by a general relevance or particularized relevance standard given the sensitive nature and potential for prejudice. It applies across all recipients (elementary, secondary, postsecondary). The Department declines to expand protections beyond evidence related to complainants' sexual interests or prior sexual conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted exceptions to the rape-shield prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of a complainant's prior sexual conduct is permissible only in two narrow circumstances: (1) to prove that someone other than the respondent committed the alleged conduct; or (2) to prove consent when the evidence concerns specific incidents of the complainant's prior sexual conduct with the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised the rule to clarify that prior consensual sexual conduct 'does not by itself' demonstrate or imply consent to the alleged sex-based harassment. Determinations about applicability of exceptions are inherently fact-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirement on impermissible evidence (§106.8(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators, decisionmakers, and other persons responsible for implementing grievance procedures must be trained on the types of evidence that are impermissible regardless of relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required training is intended to help implement the rape-shield prohibition effectively at all education levels, including elementary and secondary schools where applying evidentiary rules may otherwise be more challenging.

rubrics_metrics.name: No criminal-trial Rule 412 exception in Title IX proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to incorporate Rule 412(b)(1)(C) (the criminal-defendant exception) or to create an exception for evidence that might be exculpatory in a criminal context; respondents in Title IX proceedings do not receive the same constitutional protections as criminal defendants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reasons that allowing the criminal exception would not present the same constitutional concerns and could import complex criminal evidentiary rules that make non-lawyers less likely to serve as decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' opportunity to challenge exclusion of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may articulate why specific evidence should not be excluded under §106.45(b)(7)(iii) as part of their reasonable opportunity to respond; recipients may allow parties to explain why evidence should not be excluded during other parts of the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in the provision vests sole control in the investigator; parties can assert relevance or applicability of an exception when given opportunity to respond. Recipients may structure where and how parties challenge exclusions (e.g., during evidence access or other procedural steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(b)(7)(iii) protections do not extend to respondents' prior sexual conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to extend rape-shield protections to respondents; prior sexual conduct by respondents is governed by the general relevance standard (see §106.2) and assessed case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern evidence regarding respondents may be admissible if objectively evaluated for relevance to the allegations. Recipients must ensure fair proceedings while permitting a broad universe of admissible evidence, limited only by the complainant-focused rape-shield restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'prior' sexual conduct for §106.45(b)(7)(iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Prior' sexual conduct refers to any conduct occurring before the conclusion of the grievance procedures and is not limited to conduct that occurred before the alleged incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with the Department's prior use of 'prior' (rather than 'other') to reference evidence unrelated to the conduct at issue. Evidence about conduct after the alleged incident falls within the prohibition if it relates to sexual conduct/interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'sexual interests' evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence related to 'sexual interests' includes, but is not limited to, mode of dress, speech, and lifestyle; the term is used in preference to 'sexual predisposition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of directly linked evidence include pregnancy, use of birth control, or a medical history of a sexually transmitted infection — such evidence is prohibited under §106.45(b)(7)(iii) unless it falls within a narrow exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(b)(8) — Limited use of different procedures for some complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient that chooses to use certain grievance procedures for some, but not all, complaints must articulate consistent principles in its written grievance procedures describing how it will determine which procedures apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must inform their education community in advance about factors they will consider (e.g., form of harassment, student ages, types of evidence). Determinations must treat complainants and respondents equitably per §106.45(b)(1). A recipient may not use different procedures for different parties within the same complaint (e.g., live hearing for one party but not the other) except for disability-related accommodations or language access services.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(c) — Timing and baseline content of the notice of allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide a notice of allegations '[u]pon initiation of the recipient's grievance procedures' that includes: identities of the parties involved, the conduct alleged to constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part, and the date(s) and location(s) of the alleged incident(s), if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiation timing allows recipients to resolve threshold issues (e.g., safety concerns, dismissal determinations) before providing notice, but the notice must be provided as soon as those issues are resolved to avoid undue delay. The Department declined to require simultaneous notice to all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(c) — Notice must inform parties of access to evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of allegations must include a statement that the parties are entitled to an equal opportunity to access the relevant and not-otherwise-impermissible evidence or an accurate description of that evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a recipient provides only a description of the evidence, the parties may request and must receive access to the relevant and not impermissible evidence under §106.45(f)(4)(i). This aligns notice content with evidence-access provisions in §106.45(f)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in notice format and audience-appropriate delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may provide notices in writing or orally depending on context and recipient type; written notice is appropriate and beneficial in many postsecondary or serious-consequence cases, but oral notice may be appropriate for elementary and secondary students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to mandate written notice for elementary and secondary schools to allow prompt, developmentally appropriate responses. Recipients must nonetheless document notices (see §106.8(f)). Recipients may reduce oral notices to writing at their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of notices and grievance responses (§106.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to maintain records documenting their response to complaints of sex discrimination, which includes documentation of the notice of allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping supports transparency, enforcement, and the option to reduce notices to writing when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45(d) — Permissive dismissal standard and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may permissively dismiss a complaint when appropriate, including when the alleged conduct did not occur under the recipient's education program or activity; conduct outside the program/activity may be dismissed because Title IX and the part do not apply outside that scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient's obligation still includes addressing a sex-based hostile environment occurring under its program even when some contributing conduct occurred off-campus or outside the United States. Recipients have discretion in terminology (they need not use the word 'dismissal') so long as they effectively convey circumstances in which they may decline to initiate or continue an investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of mandatory dismissal at the investigation outset
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to dismiss complaints at the outset based on an initial determination about whether the conduct meets the definition of sex discrimination; dismissal need not be mandatory prior to investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department concluded mandatory dismissal could prematurely foreclose investigation of complaints where additional facts could show Title IX applicability. Recipients should be permitted to conduct further investigation before deciding whether dismissal is appropriate.
